documents.title: Introduction
documents.description: What zerolog is, why its API avoids allocations, and where these docs come from.
documents.searchText: # introduction {#introduction} `zerolog` is a fast, simple logger dedicated to **json output**. its chaining api writes json (or cbor) events while avoiding allocations and reflection, so the hot path stays cheap under load. these docs pair short, task-oriented guides with **full go reference generated from zerolog source** at pinned commit. covers every exported package, type, function, method runnable example that ships in module. ## what optimises for {#what-zerolog-optimises-for} - **speed low allocation** on logging path. **structured output** — event object, not formatted string. **a small, composable api** `logger` events, `writer`s `hook`s extend behaviour, `level`s gate emitted. deliberately focuses efficient structured logging. human-readable console output available too, through (intentionally slower) `zerolog.consolewriter`. packages this module {#packages-in-this-module} more than root logger: `github.com/rs/zerolog` core logger, levels, fields, encoders, hooks. `github.com/rs/zerolog/log` package-level global wired `os.stderr`. `github.com/rs/zerolog/hlog` `net/http` middleware attaches request. `github.com/rs/zerolog/diode` non-blocking writer drops saturation. `github.com/rs/zerolog/journald` systemd journal native protocol. `github.com/rs/zerolog/pkgerrors` stack-trace capture `github.com/pkg/errors`. `github.com/rs/zerolog/slog` bridge standard library `log/slog`. each package has own page **go tab, source. where come {#where-these-docs-come-from} are authored. **generated by [sourcey](https://sourcey.com)** repository using sourcey's `godoc` adapter, which reads source, doc comments `example` functions directly. build reproducible: source single commit exact command recorded evidence shipped docs.

documents.title: Quickstart
documents.description: Install zerolog and emit your first structured JSON log line.
documents.searchText: # quickstart {#quickstart} ## install {#install} ```bash go get -u github.com/rs/zerolog/log ``` simple logging {#simple-logging} import the global logger package, `github.com/rs/zerolog/log`: ```go package main ( "github.com/rs/zerolog" "github.com/rs/zerolog/log" ) func main() { // unix time is faster and smaller than most timestamp formats. zerolog.timefieldformat = zerolog.timeformatunix log.print("hello world") } ```text {"time":1516134303,"level":"debug","message":"hello world"} `log.print` writes to `os.stderr` defaults `trace` level, so a plain `log.info(...)` call appears on stderr out of box. contextual {#contextual-logging} attach strongly typed key/value pairs an event. chain must end in `msg` or `msgf`, otherwise nothing written: log.debug(). str("scale", "833 cents"). float64("interval", 833.09). msg("fibonacci everywhere") str("name", "tom"). send() {"level":"debug","scale":"833 cents","interval":833.09,"time":1562212768,"message":"fibonacci everywhere"} {"level":"debug","name":"tom","time":1562212768} levelled {#levelled-logging} zerolog.setgloballevel(zerolog.infolevel) log.info().msg("hello {"time":1516134303,"level":"info","message":"hello levels, from highest lowest: `panic`, `fatal`, `error`, `warn`, `info`, `debug`, `trace`. use `zerolog.disabled` turn off entirely. next {#next} - [context hooks](/context-and-hooks.html) for request-scoped loggers hooks. [outputs sinks](/outputs-and-sinks.html) console output, cbor samplers. **go api** tab generated reference every package.

documents.title: Context and hooks
documents.description: Request-scoped loggers, context.Context integration and hooks in zerolog.
documents.searchText: # context and hooks {#context-and-hooks} ## deriving child loggers {#deriving-child-loggers} a `logger` is cheap to copy, so build base logger once derive children with `.with()`: ```go := zerolog.new(os.stdout).with().timestamp().logger() reqlog base.with().str("request_id", id).logger() reqlog.info().msg("handling request") ``` `with()` returns `context` whose fields are copied into every event the writes. context.context integration {#contextcontext-integration} zerolog stores inside `context.context` `logger.withcontext(ctx)` reads it back `zerolog.ctx(ctx)`: ctx = logger.withcontext(ctx) log zerolog.ctx(ctx).with().str("component", "worker").logger() `*zerolog.logger` implements directly, can be passed where expected. `zerolog.ctx` disabled instead of `nil` when holds none, which keeps call sites free nil checks. {#hooks} `hook` runs on event, letting you enrich, sample or route messages. implement interface: type hook interface { run(e *zerolog.event, level zerolog.level, message string) } attached through `logger.hook(...)` global `zerolog.addglobalhook(...)`. `pkgerrors` package ships that records stack trace from `github.com/pkg/errors` value error events. http middleware {#http-middleware} `hlog` provides `net/http` injects request exposes helpers for ids remote addresses: h hlog.newhandler(log.logger) hlog.accesshandler(func(r *http.request, status, size int, dur time.duration) /* ... */ }) r hlog.remoteaddrhandler("ip") see page in **go api** tab full handler set.

documents.title: Outputs and sinks
documents.description: Console writing, non-blocking writers, CBOR encoding and sampling.
documents.searchText: # outputs and sinks {#outputs-and-sinks} ## writers {#writers} a `logger` writes to any `io.writer` via `zerolog.new(w)`. wrap or fan out the writer change where events land. `zerolog.multilevelwriter` interface sends each level different writer: ```go mw := zerolog.multilevelwriter(consolewriter, os.stdout) logger zerolog.new(mw).with().timestamp().logger() ``` pretty console output {#pretty-console-output} `zerolog.consolewriter` renders for human at terminal. it is intentionally slower than json path meant development: consolewriter zerolog.consolewriter{out: os.stderr, timeformat: time.rfc3339} zerolog.new(consolewriter).with().timestamp().logger() non-blocking {#non-blocking-writer} `diode` package provides that buffers records on ring buffer drops them once full, so slow sink never blocks application: wr diode.newwriter(os.stdout, 1000, 10*time.millisecond, func(missed int) { fmt.printf("dropped %d messages\n", missed) }) zerolog.new(wr) binary encoding {#binary-encoding} zerolog can emit cbor instead of json. set encoder level: zerolog.encoder = &zerolog.cborencoder{} this pairs with `journald` package, whose frames in systemd journal native protocol. sampling {#sampling} reduces log volume while preserving error visibility. `zerolog.sampler` combines basic-rate sampler per-level sampler: sampled log.sample(&zerolog.basicsampler{n: 10}) `levelsampler` lets keep sample rate. see `zerolog.sampler`, `basicsampler` entries go api tab.

documents.title: diode
documents.description: Package diode provides a thread-safe, lock-free, non-blocking io.Writer wrapper.
documents.searchText: package diode provides a thread-safe, lock-free, non-blocking io.writer wrapper. ## newwriter ```go func newwriter(w io.writer, size int, pollinterval time.duration, f alerter) writer ``` creates wrapping w with many-to-one in order to never block log producers and drop events if the can't keep up flow of data. use diode.writer when wr := diode.newwriter(w, 1000, 0, func(missed int) { log.printf("dropped %d messages", missed) }) zerolog.new(wr) is greater than poller used otherwise waiter used. see code.cloudfoundry.org/go-diodes for more info on diode. ### example: diode.newwriter(os.stdout, fmt.printf("dropped messages\n", zerolog.new(w) log.print("test") w.close() } output: ```text {"level":"debug","message":"test"} alerter type struct // contains filtered or unexported fields wrapper that uses make write thread safe. close (dw writer) close() error releases call wrapped io.closer implemented. write(p []byte) (n err error)
